summary: 1919 steel Aermotor LS-40 lookout on Stillwater Mountain, Herkimer County; restored by volunteers and the DEC, reopened 2016, closed each autumn to December 20.

access.note: Open to the public. The tower and most of the trail are on the Big Moose Conservation Easement (private land); visitors may use the trail but may not trespass. The trail and summit close from the second Tuesday in October through December 20.

visit.trail_note: Trail ascends 1.2 miles and 550 feet from the Big Moose Road trailhead (DEC map); the Explorer says one mile.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Verplanck Colvin built a tower on the summit, per the Adirondack Explorer. Colvin's tower is gone; the Register and Forest Lookouts begin the lookout history in 1912.
First lookout on the site, a timber tower (Register); Conservation Commission lookout station (Forest Lookouts)
Current 47-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower erected by the Conservation Commission
New cabin for the observer's living quarters constructed
Fire observation ended; Forest Lookouts says the tower was discontinued, and the Explorer says it has not been used for fire observation since
Volunteer group that later restored the tower began, per a 2016 letter
Restoration completed; reopened to the public July 2, 2016
State nominated the structure for the National Register of Historic Places; listing date not confirmed in pages read
Volunteers completed a roof repair on June 21

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Explorer credits Colvin with a tower on the summit in 1882. The Register and Forest Lookouts begin the lookout history with a 1912 timber tower, and both date the current steel tower to 1919. The story keeps the 1882 claim attributed to the Explorer.
The Register gives the current tower as 47 feet (14.3 m), which matches the record. The Explorer says fifty-six feet. The story uses the Register's figure and reports the disagreement.
The Register gives 2,244 ft (684 m) for the site. The Friends' website and the DEC map give 2,264 feet for the summit. The record keeps the Register's 684 m, and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Seasonal closure: the DEC map says the trail and summit close from the second Tuesday in October through December 20. Our count puts the 2026 start at Tuesday October 13, which is five days after the research date. Confirm with DEC or the Friends before anyone plans a visit. The Friends' homepage banner (closed until December 20, 2025) is stale. The record's 2017 NRHP listing is not confirmed: the Explorer reports only that the state nominated the structure, and the NRHP nomination PDF was not read. The 1882 Colvin tower rests on one source (the Explorer); the Forest Lookouts page and the Register begin in 1912 and do not mention it. Trail length differs: 1.2 miles (DEC) vs one mile (Explorer, Friends). Staffing is from a December 2017 Register visit report only; no current staffing was found. No photos added. The Explorer photo credit (Nancy Ford) is not reusable without permission. Pages read: 8 (including one 403 that failed) plus two web searches; the Explorer and DEC map were read last and carry the access and history claims.
